findings.pdf_says: LC_ALL    Locale-categories LC_COLLATE, LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, and LC_TIME, and any other categories included in the locale.
findings.markdown_says:
| LC_ALL | Locale-categories LC_COLLATE, LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY, |

LC_NUMERIC, and LC_TIME, and any other categories included in the locale.
findings.why_it_matters: The LC_ALL row's 'Behavior affected' cell is cut at the line wrap; the rest (LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME and 'any other categories included in the locale') sits outside the table as a free-standing paragraph, so the table row understates what LC_ALL covers.

Category Field name Description

LC_MONETARY

| int_curr_symbol | international currency symbol |
|---|---|

findings.why_it_matters: The single three-column 8.2.1 locale field-name table is shattered into a header line of plain text, three separate two-column tables and loose paragraphs (mon_decimal_point, mon_thousands_sep, n_cs_precedes); the Category column is lost as a column, so field-to-category association and the field/description pairing depend on reading order rather than table structure.

findings.pdf_says: p_cs_precedes    indicator of whether the currency symbol precedes or succeeds the value for a nonnegative quantity

findings.why_it_matters: The p_cs_precedes description is cut mid-phrase in the table cell and its ending 'a nonnegative quantity' is detached as a stray paragraph, so the cell does not say which quantity (nonnegative vs negative, the distinction from n_cs_precedes) it applies to.
